comments: Opened a bug fix. I mentioned ["partially fixes" in the PR](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/99382) because there is still the issue of the test suite timing out instead of finishing with an error.

I think the simplest way to fix the timeout issue is to move `org.elasticsearch.compute.operator.DriverRunner#runToCompletion(org.elasticsearch.threadpool.ThreadPool, int, java.util.List<org.elasticsearch.compute.operator.Driver>)` into the test suite (it's not called by any production code) and then add a timeout to the `.actionGet()`.

The timeout occurs because we don't catch Throwables but only Exceptions in AbstractRunnable, and the Driver threw a Throwable, leading to the listener in `Driver#schedule` never being notified. 

However, I don't think we should catch and rethrow Throwable in Driver. Let's add the timeout to `DriverRunner#runToCompletion`, as David suggested. I will raise a PR for this.

review_comments: I think it's worth adding a test case that reproduces this one every time. And probably explaining why we want this statement rather than a link to the bug. It takes a bit of digging to reverse the sequence of events from the bug but it's fast to read a one liner like "no nulls, it's all true." Actually, do we only get here if everything is `true`? Maybe we should just return a constant block in that case?

Hehe, yeah I had that one liner but I discarded it and used the bug url. I've removed the url and added the one-liner. Regarding the test, you are right, I rushed it; I found a specific test that uncovers this.
